**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/01 (Mon) 11:38
- [FACT] User has a 20-gallon freshwater aquarium.
- [FACT] User has a mix of neon tetras, harlequin rasboras, and a pair of fancy guppies in their aquarium.
- [FACT] User's aquarium has been set up for about 2 weeks.
- [FACT] User has noticed a greenish algae bloom growing on the glass and decorations for about a week.
- [CHANGE] User made some adjustments to the lighting in their aquarium recently.
- [PREFERENCE] User is currently using a high-quality flake food as the main staple for their fish.
- [PREFERENCE] User supplements their fish's diet with frozen brine shrimp and bloodworms.
- [FACT] User has not tested their water parameters recently but plans to do so soon.
- [FACT] User has a standard aquarium filter and cleans it every 2 weeks.
- [FACT] User is not using any algae-preventing products currently.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested that excess nutrients from the cycling process, overfeeding, insufficient biological filtration, inadequate water changes, lighting, and overcrowding could be potential causes of the algae bloom.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended monitoring and adjusting feeding to prevent overfeeding.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested performing a 25-50% water change every week to remove excess nutrients and waste products.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised checking and adjusting water parameters, including ammonia, nitrite, nitrate, pH, and temperature.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended optimizing lighting by reducing duration or intensity to prevent promoting algae growth.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested adding live plants to help absorb excess nutrients and reduce algae growth.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mentioned that beneficial bacteria supplements can help maintain a healthy balance of bacteria in the tank.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested considering upgrading to a canister filter for improved mechanical and biological filtration, better water circulation, and customization options.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised that canister filters can help with algae control by removing waste and excess nutrients.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested adding more plants to the tank to help control algae growth and improve water quality.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended choosing low-maintenance plants like Java moss, Anacharis, and Water Wisteria.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised to consider the lighting conditions when selecting plants for the aquarium.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested introducing plants gradually to the tank.
